```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thiel_2018_diclofenac_painrelief"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41540-018-0062-3> (open access; npj
  Systems Biology and Applications 4:28)
* Supplementary information (Tables S1-S4, Figures S1-S3): linked from the
  article page.

Thiel et al. (2018) coupled PK-Sim whole-body PBPK models of celecoxib,
diclofenac, licofelone, zileuton and rifampicin to two published cellular
network models: the arachidonic-acid metabolism network of Yang et al. (2007,
PLoS Comput Biol 3:e55) and the rifampicin / PXR CYP3A4 induction model of
Yamashita et al. (2013, PLoS One 8:e70330). The paper then related the
predicted decrease in prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) to the pain relief observed in
two post-oral-surgery trials, one of diclofenac and one of celecoxib, with a
sigmoid Hill equation per drug.

This package holds those two exposure-response models:

```{r models}
mod_dfn <- readModelDb("Thiel_2018_diclofenac_painrelief")
mod_cel <- readModelDb("Thiel_2018_celecoxib_painrelief")
```

* Diclofenac: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_dfn)$description`
* Celecoxib: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_cel)$description`

The PBPK models and the cellular network are not part of this package. The
PBPK models were built in PK-Sim, whose organ volumes, blood flows, tissue
partition coefficients and enzyme abundances come from the software's
database rather than from the paper; the cellular network is the Yang 2007
model used unchanged. The pain-relief models therefore take the PGE2 change as
an input, the time-varying covariate `PGE2_DELTA` (drug-treated minus drug-free
PGE2, umol/L, negative for a decrease). Inside the model the paper's
positive-for-suppression axis is recovered as `pge2_decr <- -PGE2_DELTA`.

# Population

The PGE2 trajectories were simulated for one PBPK reference individual, a
European man of 73 kg aged 30 years, after a dissolved oral dose (Thiel 2018
Methods). The pain relief data came from two trials in moderate-to-severe pain
after oral (dental) surgery (Thiel 2018 Methods, *Correlation of predicted
decrease in prostaglandin formation with pain relief*):

* Diclofenac potassium 25, 50 and 100 mg single oral doses, 197 patients
  (n = 63, 68 and 66), Hersh et al. 2004 (Thiel 2018 reference 27).
* Celecoxib 400 mg single oral dose, 57 patients, Cheung et al. 2007
  (Thiel 2018 reference 26).

Each fit used the arm-mean pain relief score at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2,
3, 4, 5 and 6 h minus the placebo-arm mean at the same time. The models are
arm-mean models; no between-subject variability was estimated.

```{r population}
str(mod_dfn()$population)
str(mod_cel()$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Diclofenac | Celecoxib | Source location |
|----------------------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| `score = emax * x^hill / (ec50^hill + x^hill)` | n/a | n/a | Results, *Correlation of predicted decrease in prostaglandin formation with pain relief*: "the Hill equation ((a*x^b)/(c^b + x^b))" |
| `x = pge2_decr = -PGE2_DELTA` (umol/L) | n/a | n/a | Figure 5 x-axis "PGE2 decrease [umol/l]"; Methods "difference of PGE2 concentrations between the drug-free treatment and the drug-treated case" |
| `score` = placebo-adjusted mean pain relief | n/a | n/a | Figure 5 y-axis "Delta(mean pain relief score, placebo)"; Methods "difference between mean pain relief scores ... and the respective placebo effects" |
| `emax` (`a`) | 2.8 (95% CI 2.0-3.5) | 2 (1.9-2.1) | Results, same paragraph |
| `hill` (`b`) | 4.4 (2.6-6.3) | 5.7 (3.7-7.8) | Results, same paragraph |
| `ec50` (`c`, umol/L) | 37.2 (31.9-42.5) | 43.4 (40.6-46.1) | Results, same paragraph; units from Figure 5 |
| `addSd` (score units) | 0.21 | 0.10 | Supplementary Table S4, rows 'DFN (6h) Hill (3)' and 'CEL (6h) Hill (3)', RMSE |

Supplementary Table S4 also prints the fit SSE (diclofenac 1.30, celecoxib
0.08), which the checks below use.

# Digitised Figure 5 data

The observed points and the PGE2 driver were digitised from Figure 5 of the
article. Each point of the bottom panels is one (PGE2 decrease, placebo-adjusted
pain relief) pair. The time of each point was assigned by matching its PGE2
value to the PGE2 curve of the top panel and confirmed against the raw
pain relief and placebo markers of the same panel. The three diclofenac arms
and the celecoxib arm each have 11 points (33 and 11 in total), which matches
the residual degrees of freedom implied by Table S4 (SSE / RMSE^2 = 29.5 and 8,
i.e. about 32 and 11 points for a three-parameter fit).

# Simulation

The PGE2 change is passed as the time-varying covariate `PGE2_DELTA` on
observation rows; each arm is one simulated subject. The model has no
differential equations and no dosing records.

```{r simulate}
make_events <- function(d) {
  d |>
    mutate(
      id = as.integer(arm),
      evid = 0L,
      PGE2_DELTA = -pge2_decr
    ) |>
    select(id, time, evid, PGE2_DELTA, arm) |>
    arrange(id, time)
}

ev_dfn <- make_events(filter(fig5, drug == "diclofenac"))
ev_cel <- make_events(filter(fig5, drug == "celecoxib"))

sim_dfn <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_dfn, events = ev_dfn, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")
sim_cel <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cel, events = ev_cel, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame")

pred <- bind_rows(sim_dfn, sim_cel) |>
  select(arm, time, pge2_decr, score) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(as.character(arm), levels = levels(fig5$arm))) |>
  left_join(fig5, by = c("arm", "time", "pge2_decr"))
stopifnot(nrow(pred) == 44L, !anyNA(pred$dscore), !anyNA(pred$score))
```

The curves below are the model evaluated over a grid of PGE2 decrease values.

```{r grid}
grid_events <- function(xmax) {
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 1, length.out = 201), evid = 0L) |>
    mutate(PGE2_DELTA = -seq(0, xmax, length.out = 201))
}
curve_dfn <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_dfn, events = grid_events(60), returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(drug = "diclofenac")
curve_cel <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cel, events = grid_events(110), returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(drug = "celecoxib")
curves <- bind_rows(curve_dfn, curve_cel)
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-5-bottom, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = curves, aes(pge2_decr, score)) +
  geom_point(data = fig5, aes(pge2_decr, dscore, colour = arm, shape = arm)) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(drug, levels = c("diclofenac", "celecoxib")), scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "PGE2 decrease (umol/L)",
    y = "Mean pain relief score minus placebo",
    colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the bottom panels of Figure 5 of Thiel 2018 (points digitised)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Driving the models with the digitised PGE2 time course gives the
placebo-adjusted pain relief over time:

```{r figure-5-top, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
pred |>
  ggplot(aes(time)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = score, colour = "model")) +
  geom_point(aes(y = dscore, colour = "observed")) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Mean pain relief score minus placebo",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Time course behind the top panels of Figure 5 of Thiel 2018,\n",
      "placebo-adjusted (the paper plots raw scores beside placebo)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Checks

## Hill anchors

Both sides of these checks use the same parameters, so the differences are
round-off and the tolerances are tight.

```{r anchors}
anchor_events <- function(ec50) {
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0:2, evid = 0L, PGE2_DELTA = -c(0, ec50, 1e4))
}
a_dfn <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_dfn, events = anchor_events(37.2), returnType = "data.frame")
a_cel <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cel, events = anchor_events(43.4), returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(
  # No PGE2 decrease, no drug effect.
  a_dfn$score[1] == 0, a_cel$score[1] == 0,
  # Half the maximal effect at x = ec50.
  abs(a_dfn$score[2] - 2.8 / 2) < 1e-10,
  abs(a_cel$score[2] - 2.0 / 2) < 1e-10,
  # The asymptote is emax.
  abs(a_dfn$score[3] / 2.8 - 1) < 1e-6,
  abs(a_cel$score[3] / 2.0 - 1) < 1e-6
)
```

## Residual error against Supplementary Table S4

The paper's fit statistics were computed on the points plotted in Figure 5, so
the packaged parameters evaluated on the digitised points should give about
the same SSE and RMSE (RMSE = sqrt(SSE / (n - 3)), the MATLAB curve fitting
toolbox definition, and the value carried as `addSd`).

```{r rmse}
fit_stats <- pred |>
  group_by(drug) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    sse = sum((dscore - score)^2),
    rmse = sqrt(sse / (n - 3)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    sse_paper = ifelse(drug == "diclofenac", 1.30, 0.08),
    rmse_paper = ifelse(drug == "diclofenac", 0.21, 0.10)
  )

fit_stats |>
  rename(
    "Drug" = drug,
    "Points" = n,
    "SSE (digitised)" = sse,
    "SSE (Table S4)" = sse_paper,
    "RMSE (digitised)" = rmse,
    "RMSE (Table S4)" = rmse_paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Fit statistics on the digitised Figure 5 points.")

# Measured 0.208 vs 0.21 (diclofenac) and 0.106 vs 0.10 (celecoxib). A 10%
# error in ec50 or emax raises the RMSE to 0.27-0.34 (diclofenac) or
# 0.19-0.20 (celecoxib), and swapping the two drugs' parameter sets to
# 0.74-0.82, so the 0.02 bound fails on a transcription error.
stopifnot(all(abs(fit_stats$rmse - fit_stats$rmse_paper) < 0.02))
```

## Refit to the digitised points

A least-squares refit of the Hill equation to the digitised points should land
inside the 95% confidence intervals the paper prints.

```{r refit}
hill_fn <- function(x, a, b, c) a * x^b / (c^b + x^b)
refit <- function(d, start) {
  stats::coef(stats::nls(dscore ~ hill_fn(pge2_decr, a, b, c), data = d, start = start))
}
est_dfn <- refit(filter(fig5, drug == "diclofenac"), list(a = 2.8, b = 4.4, c = 37.2))
est_cel <- refit(filter(fig5, drug == "celecoxib"), list(a = 2, b = 5.7, c = 43.4))

ci <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~param, ~paper, ~lower, ~upper,
  "diclofenac", "a (emax)", 2.8, 2.0, 3.5,
  "diclofenac", "b (hill)", 4.4, 2.6, 6.3,
  "diclofenac", "c (ec50)", 37.2, 31.9, 42.5,
  "celecoxib", "a (emax)", 2.0, 1.9, 2.1,
  "celecoxib", "b (hill)", 5.7, 3.7, 7.8,
  "celecoxib", "c (ec50)", 43.4, 40.6, 46.1
) |>
  mutate(refit = c(est_dfn, est_cel))

ci |>
  rename(
    "Drug" = drug, "Parameter" = param, "Paper" = paper,
    "95% CI lower" = lower, "95% CI upper" = upper, "Refit" = refit
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Refit to the digitised points against the published estimates.")

stopifnot(all(ci$refit > ci$lower & ci$refit < ci$upper))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- The PGE2 change is an input. In the paper it is the output of the Yang 2007
  arachidonic-acid network (human polymorphonuclear leukocytes) with
  competitive COX-2 inhibition (Ki 0.018 for diclofenac, 0.017 for celecoxib,
  converted from literature IC50 values), driven by the PK-Sim prediction of
  the unbound drug concentration in venous blood cells. Neither layer is in
  this package, so the models cannot be dosed; a user must supply
  `PGE2_DELTA` from their own prediction of the network. Its umol/L scale is
  the network's internal concentration scale, not a PGE2 immunoassay value.
- The maintainers registered the covariate as the signed change
  `PGE2_DELTA` (negative = decrease), matching the existing `LDLC_DELTA`
  biomarker-change canonical, and recover the paper's decrease inside the
  model. The models are defined for a decrease (`PGE2_DELTA <= 0`); a positive
  value makes the non-integer Hill power undefined and returns `NaN`.
- The fits are to arm means over time, pooled across doses for diclofenac. The
  link is direct (no delay), as fitted. No between-subject variability was
  estimated, and `addSd` is the residual SD of the arm-mean fit, not a
  per-patient residual.
- The Figure 5 points were digitised by the maintainers from the published
  raster at about 0.2 umol/L and 0.01 score units per pixel. They are used only
  for the checks above; no model value comes from them.
- Not included: the 24 h celecoxib fit (Supplementary Table S4 gives its fit
  statistics, RMSE 0.22, but the paper does not report its parameters); the
  drug efficacy score (Equation 1), which combines PGE2 and omega-hydroxy-LTB4
  outputs of the network; and the licofelone and zileuton results, for which
  the paper had no time-resolved clinical data to relate to an outcome.
- No correction notice for the article was found (checked October 2026).
